title: A Bloom filter says maybe
description: The URL-seen Bloom filter has a 1% false-positive rate. It says a newly discovered URL may already be present. This crawl values completeness enough to pay for extra metadata lookups. How should the scheduler use that answer?

options.text: Skip the URL because a positive Bloom-filter result proves it was fetched.
options.explanation: A positive is only a possible match. Skipping it accepts the risk of missing a genuinely new URL.

options.text: Confirm positive results in the exact seen store; treat negative results as definitely absent from the filter's inserted set.
options.explanation: Exact confirmation protects completeness when the filter says maybe. Properly maintained Bloom filters have false positives, not false negatives; durable seen-state handling still matters.

options.text: Fetch every positive result again and ignore the metadata store.
options.explanation: Most positives may be genuinely seen URLs. Re-fetching them wastes bandwidth and host budgets instead of checking the ambiguity cheaply.

options.text: Use the page's SimHash to decide whether the URL has been seen before fetching it.
options.explanation: SimHash describes fetched content, which is not yet available. URL dedupe and near-duplicate content detection answer different questions.
